request: Create an APB GPIO peripheral with interrupts.
expected_behavior: RTL for module apb_gpio (APB4, ADDR_WIDTH 8, 32-bit data, zero wait states, N pins with N 8 by default and 1 to 32 allowed) with DATA_OUT, DIR, a read-only DATA_IN, rising, falling, high and low detection enables, an interrupt enable mask and a write-1-to-clear INTR_STATUS at 0x00 to 0x20, a level irq, and a self-checking testbench, following the approved interface specification and microarchitecture, gated by lint, simulation, and synthesis (and formal, when a .sby is written) before review. Every read-back register, DATA_IN included, is 0 straight after reset, never unknown.
constraints: Work only from the approved interface specification and microarchitecture.
Correct for every N from 1 to 32: bits N and up read as zero and ignore writes.
Lint-clean under Verilator -Wall with no waivers.
known_failure_modes: DATA_IN reads unknown (X) after reset because the input sample register is not reset, or loads only under an enable that is never reset (seen in two live trials of rtl/apb-gpio, one with and one without knowledge documents).
A self-written testbench that compares read-back values with != or ==, so an unknown value never raises an error; the must-fail control fails it.

held_out.name: The reference testbench passes on the seat's RTL
The seat's testbench fails a design whose DATA_IN is unknown after reset
